title: Key Lifecycle, Rotation, Invalidation, and Attestation Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies key lifecycle, rotation, invalidation, and attestation?
options: Version ciphertext and keys, migrate idempotently, distinguish loss from corruption, and verify attestation server-side with fresh binding.
Delete the old key before migration
Trust an attestation chain entirely on-device
Use an alias without format metadata
questions.answer: Version ciphertext and keys, migrate idempotently, distinguish loss from corruption, and verify attestation server-side with fresh binding.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Successful key attestation permanently proves that every future request from the device is trustworthy.
questions.explanation: Regenerating a missing alias under the same name hides key loss and makes every existing record permanently undecryptable without a clear recovery path.

questions.prompt: Why must ciphertext carry a key or format version?
questions.answer: So decryption and resumable rotation can select the correct format and key without guessing.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
